Because I don't have access to live financial data, I can't confirm the exact top interest rates on UK current accounts right now, as banks adjust their offers frequently based on the Bank of England base rate.

However, the UK current accounts that consistently offer the highest interest rates—and the exact catch to watch out for with each—generally fall into three categories:

1. High-Interest Current Accounts (Best for smaller balances)

Several major high-street and digital banks pay competitive interest directly on your main current account balance, though they almost always cap the amount of money that earns that rate.

Nationwide FlexDirect: Historically one of the strongest performers for new customers, offering a high introductory interest rate for the first 12 months on balances up to £1,500 (provided you pay in a minimum amount each month, usually £1,000+).

Santander Edge / Edge Up: These accounts pay solid in-credit interest on much larger balances (up to £4,000 on Edge, or up to £25,000 on Edge Up) alongside cashback on household bills. However, they come with a monthly account fee, so you need to hold a decent balance to make the interest outweigh the fee.

Kroo: A digital current account that tracks the Bank of England base rate, paying interest on balances up to £85,000 with no monthly fee or minimum deposit requirements—making it one of the simplest options for larger sums.

Chase UK: Offers a current account with 1% cashback on everyday debit card spending, paired with an easy-access "saver" account linked directly inside the app that pays a competitive variable rate on larger balances.

2. Linked Regular Savers (Highest headline rates)

If you hold a current account with banks like First Direct, Nationwide, Lloyds, NatWest, or Santander, you unlock access to their exclusive "Regular Saver" accounts.

These routinely offer the highest interest rates on the market (often 6% to 7%+ AER).

The catch: You can only deposit a small amount each month (typically between £25 and £300), and the rate usually lasts for just 12 months before dropping.

3. Under-18s & Youth Current Accounts

If you are under 18, standard adult current accounts won't be available to you, and youth accounts rarely pay high interest on main balances. Instead, banks like Nationwide (FlexOne), Santander (123 Mini), and TSB (Under 19s) offer low-to-moderate interest on current account balances, while pairing them with Youth Regular Savers or Junior ISAs (from providers like Coventry Building Society or Nationwide) that offer much higher tax-free interest rates.

Because banks change these rates weekly, check a live comparison table before applying—MoneySavingExpert (MSE) updates their "Best Bank Accounts" and "Top Savings Accounts" guides daily with the exact current rates and eligibility rules.
